title: Feasibility study on OPD diagnostics for couples with sexual dysfunction
summary:
Sexual dysfunctions are common and are often associated with significant distress. Relationship factors play a considerable role in their onset and maintenance. For an adequate treatment recommendation and planning, targeted diagnostics are important. The Operationalized Psychodynamic Diagnostics (OPD-3) is a well-established clinical interview procedure for the systematic assessment of psychodynamic aspects. To date, OPD-3 has not been systematically applied to couples with sexual dysfunctions.
This study examines whether the use of OPD-3 interviews with couples with sexual dysfunction within the routine clinical care of an outpatient clinic for sexual health is practically feasible and what added value it offers for diagnostics and treatment planning. Twenty couples in which at least one person suffers from a sexual dysfunction will participate in four appointments: a joint initial consultation, two individual OPD-3 interviews, and a final session.
conditions: Sexual dysfunction, not caused by organic disorder or disease

interventions.name: Couples with sexual dysfunction (ICD-11) in at least one partner, recruited from the routine clinical care of an outpatient psychotherapy clinic (Institutsambulanz)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Couples (both partners aged 18-65 years)
- Presentation with symptoms of sexual dysfunction in at least one partner at the specialist outpatient clinic for sexual health and sexual medicine
- ICD-10 diagnosis of sexual dysfunction (clinical assessment)
- Relationship duration >= 6 months
- Willingness to attend 4 appointments within routine outpatient care
- Sufficient German language skills
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute psychiatric crisis or suicidality
- Acute substance dependence
- Ongoing sex therapy
- Severe cognitive impairment
